summary: The record, from `?since=<seq>`: the operator's, like `/state`. The dashboard reads this and nothing else, so it can never show a state the record does not hold. A ticket is one line when it is asked (with its token's sha256, never the token) and one for each thing that happens to it - offered, claimed as a rental, given up, dropped, released, taken back - never a line per wait, so a ticket waiting an hour does not bury the record. A rental's processes are one line whenever its list changes (`rental_processes`, the whole list after the change), never one per heartbeat. A rental that lapsed is one line when it is taken back (`rental_reclaiming`), one for each process it named - `process_ended`, `process_gone` (already gone), `process_left_alone` (alive, but not carrying its proof: its pid belongs to something else now, or its command line could not be read) or `process_not_ended` (ended and not gone within its bound, or not endable) - and one when the card is free again (`rental_reclaimed`). A release is one line when it is asked (`rental_releasing`, with what the rental names), one for each straggler it ends, named the same way, and one when the card is free again (`rental_released`) - so a coordinator stopped in the middle of a release rebuilds the rental as being given back, and finishes it. The memory is on the record with its numbers (`memory`): a ticket refused for it - an ask that could never fit, or a claim that did not fit (`ticket_refused`) - a scheduled ticket passed over until the card has the room (`ticket_passed_over`, once each time it is passed over), and each model a rental adds, approved (`rental_amended`) or refused (`amend_refused`). So is the machine's card lock: the coordinator waiting for it while an application run on its own has the card (`lock_waiting`), and taking it (`lock_taken`). Every line served is in the event shape: a line an older coordinator wrote in a shape since replaced - the turns tickets replaced (`turn_*`), a rental's one process (`rental_process`) - stays in the file, is left out here, and the start line says how many there are. THE WATCH is on the record too (PLAN-4 D3): a rental that said it was working and whose progress did not move for the hang limit is one line when it is found (`rental_hung`, saying why), then taken back as a lapsed one is; a rental whose card is over-full is one line when it is marked degraded (`rental_degraded`, with the `degraded` it was told - why, and the numbers) and one when the card has room again (`rental_restored`) - never a line per look at the card, nor per heartbeat. A rental marked degraded for a memory error its models' logs said says, on its line, how many its heartbeats had said since its grant (`memory_errors`): a coordinator restarted takes that count - or 0, for a rental with no such line - as what its holder has already said, so an error said first on the heartbeat after the restart is news, and marked. A line with no count (an older coordinator's) leaves it unknown: the first heartbeat's count after the restart is then taken as known.
